text:
The Blues were down 4-2 early in the third period at Little Caesars Arena, and they finished the night ahead 5-4. Justin Barron tied it at 12:57, and 18 seconds later Aleksanteri Kaskimaki scored the first NHL goal of his career. The Blues took the lead on what turned out to be the winner, tipping the puck in off assists from Alexey Toropchenko and Pius Suter. Kaskimaki was a 73rd overall pick in 2022, and he arrived in the NHL after 63 games in Springfield last season.

It was close all night by the numbers we trust. Expected goals (the quality of chances, not the count of shots) finished STL 2.3, DET 2.06, and our deserved-to-win figure, the share of simulated replays each team wins, gave the Blues 53 percent. Detroit had the better first period and the Blues the better second, when they out-chanced the Wings 1.02 to 0.6, though Lucas Raymond and Keegan Kolesar had both scored by then. Detroit also outshot St. Louis 28-15 on goal. The Blues' goals came on a steady diet of tip-ins and snap shots, and Robert Thomas had a 27 percent look in the third that John Gibson stopped.

Gibson was the difference. He allowed 2.8 goals more than the 15 shots against him should have cost, and Joel Hofer was also below expectation, 1.94 goals worse than the chances he faced. The Wings got a power-play goal from Emmitt Finnie that made it 4-2, but they went quiet after that. The facts we have don't include standings or streaks for either club, so all we can say is that St. Louis walked out with a comeback win and Detroit with the sort of loss that sticks, given the lead it blew.
